Define a function with a custom gradient

Source: R/api_misc.R
custom_gradient.Rd

Port of jax.custom_gradient: fun returns list(value, vjp) where vjp(g) maps the output cotangent to the input cotangents (a list with one entry per argument, or the cotangent itself when fun has a single argument). Built on custom_vjp(); the values vjp closes over are saved as residuals.

Usage

custom_gradient(fun, with_logs = FALSE, with_accums = NULL)

Arguments

fun

A function returning list(value, vjp).

with_logs

Whether vjp also returns logs.

with_accums

NULL, or the accumulator kinds vjp receives.

Value

A function returning value, differentiated with vjp.

Details

With with_logs = TRUE, vjp(g) returns list(in_cts, logs), where logs is a named list of values to log out of the backward pass or NULL (see custom_vjp_defvjp_with_logs()). With with_accums, vjp(g, ...) takes one gradient accumulator per argument (with the structure of the arguments) instead of returning cotangents, and returns NULL or a named list of logs. with_accums declares the kind of each accumulator: a tree prefix of the list of arguments with leaves ad_ValAccum or ad_RefAccum. Arguments that are not differentiated (including integer ones) get a NullAccum whatever is declared.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
f <- custom_gradient(function(x) list(x^2, function(g) g * x))
grad(f)(3)  # 3, not 6
f <- custom_gradient(function(x) list(x^2, function(g) list(2 * g * x, list(ct = g))),
                     with_logs = TRUE)
vjp(f, 3)[[2]]$with_logs(1)
} # }
